coverage_note: § 23 a, § 38 and § 42 a, where time is the form of sensibility and the unity of the stream. The other 27 sections with term hits, among them § 39 and § 42 b, are not extracted; the free-variation chapters named in gap-007 are outside this pass.

units.claim: Simple apprehension is an egoic activity living within the passive flow of time-consciousness, its object a unity in immanent time enduring through the streaming phases of perception.
units.quote: But it is an activity that lives within the passive flow of time-consciousness. The object, as perceived, is a unity in immanent time: it endures through the streaming phases of perception, continuously identified as the same.

units.claim: The still-holding-in-grasp of what was just given is called a form of passivity within the activity of apprehending, a retentional consciousness that is not an active achievement.
units.quote: This still-holding-in-grasp is a form of passivity within the activity of apprehending. The object does not simply vanish when a new phase appears; it is retained in a modified manner, still belonging to the ongoing perception as a just-past phase of the same object.

units.term: horizon of the before and after
units.claim: Every perception is said to have its horizon of the before and after, pointing back to what was previously perceived and presentifiable in memories.
units.quote: Every perception, as consciousness meaning actual objectuality, has its horizon of the before and after.

units.claim: Everything originally appearing, even in conflict, has its determinate time-position - an immanent phenomenal time and a fixed position in the one objective time.
units.quote: Hence everything originally appearing, even if it appears in conflict, has its determinate time-position — not only an immanent phenomenal time in the intentional objectuality as such, but also its fixed position in the one objective time.

units.claim: The Kantian thesis that time is the form of sensibility is endorsed as the inner truth: time is the first and fundamental form, the form of all forms and presupposition of all other unity-founding connections.
units.quote: We now understand the inner truth of the Kantian thesis: time is the form of sensibility, and therefore it is the form of every possible world of objective experience.

units.claim: Temporality as duration, coexistence and succession is the necessary form of all unitarily intuitable objects, and form of intuition carries a second sense of temporal orientation in a presence.
units.quote: Temporality as duration, coexistence, and succession is the necessary form of all unitarily intuitable objects and, insofar, their form of intuition.

units.claim: In empathy an intersubjectively common objective time is constituted, into which everything individual in experiences and intentional objectualities must be orderable.
units.quote: In it, an intersubjectively common objective time is constituted, into which everything individual — in experiences and in intentional objectualities — must be able to be ordered.

units.claim: The time-connection is named as the connection that makes possible the unity of all perceptions and positional presentifications of an ego, established in the sphere of passivity.
units.quote: the time-connection has been brought out as this connection. It is established in the sphere of passivity — that is, in sensibility.

units.claim: All experiences of an ego are constituted in the absolute flow of inner time-consciousness, with their absolute position and unique occurrence in the absolute now, whence they retentionally sink.
units.quote: All experiences of an ego have their temporal unity; they are constituted in the absolute flow of inner time-consciousness and have in it their absolute position and uniqueness, their unique occurrence in the absolute now, whereupon they retentionally fade and sink into the past.

units.claim: The time of the experiences is distinguished from the time of the intentional objectualities: the remembered is past and far removed while the remembering is simultaneous with the perceiving.
units.quote: But the remembered is past and even "far removed" from the perceived (a character that is not an immediately intuitive time-character but points to an unfolding in chains of intuitions), while the memory as experience is simultaneous with the perceptual experience.
